questions.question: State the accounting equation and define each of its three elements, with one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A = OE + L. Assets: resources owned by the business that bring future benefits, e.g. bank, equipment, trading stock. Owner's equity: the owner's claim on the business (capital plus profit less drawings), e.g. capital contributed. Liabilities: debts owed to outsiders, e.g. a bank loan.

questions.question: Analyse the effect on the accounting equation, with reasons: (a) the owner withdrew R1 000 cash for personal use; (b) rent of R3 000 was paid by EFT; (c) equipment was bought for R8 000 by EFT.
questions.expected_answer: (a) Assets -1 000 (Bank: cash paid); OE -1 000 (drawings by owner); L 0. (b) Assets -3 000 (Bank: money paid); OE -3 000 (expense incurred: rent); L 0. (c) Assets +8 000 (Equipment bought) and -8 000 (Bank: money paid); OE 0; L 0.

questions.question: After the shop's transactions, bank is R54 500, equipment R8 000, owner's equity R47 500 and the loan R15 000. Show that the accounting equation balances.
